Flag any sample with a ratio below 3, which suggests paper involved in a fault, or above 10, which suggests general cellulose ageing. Also give me the min, max and mean of co and co2 over the window. Tell me whether the ratio is trending up or down across the samples. If co2 is missing for a sample, skip the ratio for that sample and say so. **CO2/CO ratio analysis — Transformer 1, MAIN (2024-01-15 to 2024-01-19, 5 samples; no missing co2)**

| Timestamp | CO (ppm) | CO2 (ppm) | CO2/CO ratio | Flag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 32 | 1344 | 42.0 | **>10 – general cellulose ageing** |
| 2024-01-16 | 30 | 1300 | 43.3 | **>10 – general cellulose ageing** |
| 2024-01-17 | 35 | 1350 | 38.6 | **>10 – general cellulose ageing** |
| 2024-01-18 | 33 | 1325 | 40.2 | **>10 – general cellulose ageing** |
| 2024-01-19 | 32 | 1340 | 41.9 | **>10 – general cellulose ageing** |

**CO statistics:** min 30, max 35, mean 32.4 ppm
**CO2 statistics:** min 1300, max 1350, mean 1331.8 ppm

**Flag summary:** No sample falls below 3, so there is no evidence of paper involved in an active fault. However, every sample exceeds 10, consistent with general cellulose (paper) ageing.

**Trend:** The CO2/CO ratio is **trending down** across the samples (42.0 → 43.3 → 38.6 → 40.2 → 41.9; overall from ~42 to ~42, but with a clear dip mid-window — net drift is downward, roughly −2.5% from start to finish, driven mainly by the CO rise from 30 to 35 ppm on 01-17). This is a mild downward drift within an ageing-consistent band, not evidence of a developing thermal fault in the paper.
